findings.description: No line in tests/doctor.bats has [[ or (( as its first non-whitespace token; the check detects its own failing example, returning 20 lines at the baseline.
findings.evidence:
$ /usr/bin/grep -nE '^[[:space:]]*(\[\[|\(\()' tests/doctor.bats; echo "EXIT=$?"
EXIT=1
(no output; exit 1 = no match, not exit 2 = failed to run)

Self-detection at baseline, per the diff of git show 61213fe:tests/doctor.bats against the working tree: all 20 first-token [[ lines (baseline 97, 98, 116, 134-137, 140, 156, 174, 175, 194, 195, 210, 227, 228, 243, 244, 251, 271) are gone from the converted file.

findings.description: All 20 baseline sites re-derived line by line against git show 61213fe:tests/doctor.bats: every needle is byte-identical, every haystack is still $output, every polarity is preserved, and no assertion inlines its own comparison.

(251 and 271 shift by +9 rather than +2 because baseline :244 expands to a 9-line block; verified directly: tests/doctor.bats:260 is '\tassert_contains "skipping"', :280 is '\tassert_contains "none"'.)

POLARITY, the four trap sites (baseline 140, 175, 195, 228). All four are assert_not_contains, matching their baseline !=. Proven load-bearing rather than merely present: in a scratch git worktree carrying the working-tree files, flipping each one to assert_contains turns exactly one case red and no others.
  line 142 -> assert_contains "terminal": not ok 3 names the key, the half and the cask when the registry is missing one
  line 177 -> assert_contains "none":     not ok 5 matches the whole cask name, not a prefix of a longer one
  line 197 -> assert_contains "none":     not ok 6 a cask in a bundle this machine hasn't enabled is a gap
  line 230 -> assert_contains "none":     not ok 8 an empty list is a gap on a tier that installs from Homebrew

THE DISJUNCTION, baseline :244 == *"undeclared"* || == *"casks"*, now tests/doctor.bats:250-253:
	case "$output" in
	*undeclared* | *casks*) ;;
	*) return 1 ;;
	esac
Both substrings survive, spelled with the same text. It is a plain case, not built from assert_contains calls, so tests/mutation-check.sh still counts exactly 20 enumerable doctor sites (19 helper calls at :99,100,118,136,137,138,139,142,158,176,177,196,197,212,229,230,245,260,280 plus this one construct) and neither mutation rule claims these lines.
Returns non-zero when neither matches, proven by sentinel mutation in the scratch worktree:
  *zzsentinelzz* | *qqsentinelqq*) ;;  ->  not ok 9 a half with no casks key at all is reported as undeclared
Not narrowed to the arm that passes today: dropping to *casks*) alone leaves the suite green, so a narrowing worker would have kept that arm and lost the other. Dropping to *undeclared*) alone reports not ok 9. Keeping both is what preserves the baseline condition.
Failure propagates from a non-last position under this machine's bash 3.2.57(1)-release, unlike the [[ ]] it replaces:
  $ /bin/bash -c 'set -e; f() { local output="nothing relevant"; case "$output" in *undeclared*|*casks*) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac; echo "REACHED-BAD"; }; f'
  (no output) exit=1
  $ /bin/bash -c 'set -e; f() { local output="nothing relevant"; [[ "$output" == *"undeclared"* || "$output" == *"casks"* ]]; echo "REACHED (swallowed)"; }; f'
  REACHED (swallowed) exit=0

SHARED HELPERS, not inlined comparisons: tests/doctor.bats:13 is load 'helpers'; /usr/bin/grep -cE '^[[:space:]]*(function[[:space:]]+)?(assert_contains|assert_not_contains)[[:space:]]*(\(\))?[[:space:]]*\{' tests/doctor.bats returns 0, so no local redefinition shadows the shared file. tests/helpers.bash:7-17 defines both from grep -qF and case, with haystack defaulting to "${2-$output}", so the single-argument call sites keep $output as the haystack.

REGRESSION: $ timeout 300 bats --formatter tap tests/doctor.bats -> 1..11, ok 1 through ok 11, BATS_EXIT=0. /usr/bin/grep -c '^@test' returns 11; diff of the baseline's @test lines against the current ones is empty (exit 0), so no case was renamed, deleted, or added. /usr/bin/grep -nE '^[[:space:]]*skip\b' exits 1 with no output.

SCOPE: git diff --name-only lists only tests/apps.bats, tests/doctor.bats, tests/font.bats, tests/install-failures.bats, tests/jsonc.bats, tests/licensed-fonts.bats, tests/packages.bats (plus untracked tests/helpers.bash). git diff --name-only -- . ':(exclude)tests/' is empty, and git diff --stat 61213fe -- dot_local/bin/executable_dotfiles-doctor is empty, so the doctor was not touched to make a converted assertion pass.
